clue.text: Decorating with utterly worthless material front of emporium and surround

parts.note: utterly, as in all gone, gives all
pap is soft mushy food, and by extension trivial worthless reading matter

indicators.note: front of picks out the opening letter of the word emporium

parts.note: to ring something is to surround it

explanation.surface: Someone redecorates a shop with cheap stuff on its frontage and borders.
explanation.walkthrough: 'front of' gives the E of emporium. The pieces W, ALL, PAP, E and RING run straight on in clue order; 'and' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Hanging patterned sheets on interior walls is a common form of home decoration.

clue.text: Work by Auden perhaps, a great piece of fiction

indicators.note: by means beside, so the work sits next to the poet's initials

parts.note: W.H. were the initials of the poet Auden, used here as a stand-in for him
OP, short for opus, is a musical or literary work
a as in 'ten pounds a head' means per

explanation.surface: A long Auden poem praised as a fine piece of imaginative writing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by' only places OP beside WH, and the poet's initials come first. 'a' is per, as in 'twice a day'. The definition jokes that a big lie is a great piece of fiction.
explanation.definitionFit: A whopper is slang for an outrageous lie, which is a large invention passed off as truth.

clue.text: Sky program that's infectious: one could get hooked!

parts.note: to sky a ball is to hit it high, which is to lob it
a worm is a self-spreading malicious computer program

explanation.surface: A satellite TV programme so catchy that viewers become addicted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sky' looks like the broadcaster, but here it is the verb for hitting a ball high. 'hooked' is about bait on a fishing hook, not addiction.
explanation.definitionFit: This large earthworm is a favourite angler's bait, so it ends up threaded on a hook.

clue.text: Mischievous fellow shifting purse or purses

parts.note: Puck is the mischievous sprite of A Midsummer Night's Dream

indicators.note: shifting tells us the letters of purse move around into a new order

explanation.surface: A rogue moving a purse about, or several purses, like a pickpocket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'purses' at the end is the verb, as in pursing the lips, not the plural of the wallet in the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: To purse your lips is to draw them together into a tight rounded shape, ready for a kiss.

clue.text: Bit of blooming pressure and rest is needed!

parts.note: P is the physics symbol for pressure
et al. is Latin shorthand for 'and the others', that is, and the rest

explanation.surface: Under strain at work, someone insists a break is needed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blooming' is not the British mild swear word here but flowering; 'and rest' is read as et al.
explanation.definitionFit: Each coloured leaf of a flower's corolla is one segment of the bloom.

clue.text: Female managed opponents at bridge with neat intervention

indicators.note: intervention means one piece comes between the letters of another, so the beast goes inside

parts.note: to manage a business is to run it, past tense ran
neat is an old word for cattle, and an ox is one
in bridge North and East sit on opposing sides, so N and E are opponents

explanation.surface: A woman organised her bridge rivals, with a tidy bit of interference.
explanation.walkthrough: 'neat' looks like 'tidy' but is the old word for cattle; 'intervention' puts OX inside RANNE.
explanation.definitionFit: Roxanne is a woman's given name, famously Cyrano's beloved.

clue.text: Something ornamental put on sink a hindrance

parts.note: to sink a drink, or neck it, is to swallow it quickly
let is an old word for an obstruction, as in 'without let or hindrance'

explanation.surface: Fitting a decorative fixture on a kitchen basin proves an obstacle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sink' looks like the basin, but it is slang for drinking down fast, which is also 'neck'.
explanation.definitionFit: This small ornamental band is worn around the throat, so it is jewellery one puts on.

clue.text: Piano repairer holds up hat — one I should box

parts.note: P is the musical direction for soft, piano

indicators.note: holds means the repairer's letters go round the other piece

parts.note: a righter is one who puts things right, a repairer

indicators.note: up in a down clue says the hat and the numeral are read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: a fez is a flat-topped tasselled hat
the Roman numeral I is one

explanation.surface: A piano tuner lifts his hat, and the narrator vows to fight someone.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is spoken by the boxer himself: 'I should box' sums up his trade. 'up' reverses the hat and numeral, as this is a down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A professional boxer fights for money, so boxing is what such a person is meant to do.

clue.text: Doctor in choir out of lozenges

indicators.note: in places the doctor inside the jumbled choir letters
out means the letters of choir are put out of their usual order

parts.note: MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a doctor's degree

explanation.surface: A doctor in the church choir has run out of throat sweets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lozenges' looks like cough sweets, but here it is the diamond shape, and 'of lozenges' works as an adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: A rhombus is an equal-sided parallelogram, and a lozenge is that diamond shape, so the adjective means lozenge-shaped.

clue.text: Vehicle's bill for carrying football or cricket team about

indicators.note: carrying means the bill's letters contain the team and the about

parts.note: a tab is a bill run up at a bar
both sides field eleven players, written XI
ca, for circa, means about

explanation.surface: A ride's bill grows because it carries a whole sports team around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' is circa here and reverses nothing; 'football or cricket team' is the usual crossword eleven.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a car with a meter that carries paying passengers, a hired vehicle.

clue.text: Tucking into crackers, leave desserts

indicators.note: tucking into means one piece is tucked inside the other's letters

parts.note: crackers and bananas are both slang for crazy
to split is slang for to leave

explanation.surface: Diners eating biscuits are told to abandon the pudding course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tucking into' looks like eating, and 'crackers' like biscuits; both are working parts, the first a container signal and the second slang for mad.
explanation.definitionFit: These are sweet dishes of a halved fruit with ice cream, served after a main course.

clue.text: Chapter on love poetry essential for the Washington post?

indicators.note: on in an across clue means coming after, so the chapter follows love

parts.note: love in tennis is nil, and zip is slang for nothing
an ode is a lyric poem

explanation.surface: A chapter of romantic verse is vital reading at a Washington newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Washington post' looks like the newspaper but means American mail, which needs this postal number. 'on' puts C after ZIP.
explanation.definitionFit: An American postal number is needed for mail in the US to be sorted and delivered.

clue.text: Learn bodleian periodically gets something on the fleece

indicators.note: periodically means taking letters at regular intervals, every other one from these words

explanation.surface: A student learns at Oxford's Bodleian Library, now and then, about sheep.
explanation.walkthrough: 'periodically' takes the odd letters of 'Learn bodleian'. The Bodleian is Oxford University's main library.
explanation.definitionFit: This greasy wax occurs naturally in sheep's wool and is extracted for ointments.

clue.text: Government department formerly eccentric and historically square

parts.note: FO, the Foreign Office, was a UK ministry before mergers renamed it
rum is old British slang for odd or eccentric

explanation.surface: An old ministry was odd and very old-fashioned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'square' looks like an old-fashioned person but means a public square; FO is the old Foreign Office of the UK government.
explanation.definitionFit: In ancient Rome this was the open public square used for markets and assemblies.

clue.text: Stirring around ten, quits northern French town

indicators.note: stirring around means the letters of ten and quits are mixed up

explanation.surface: Restless around ten o'clock, someone leaves a town in northern France.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stirring around' scrambles TENQUITS into STQUENTI, then N is added. 'northern' looks part of the place description but supplies the last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a town in Picardy, in the north of France.

clue.text: Tremble and flee clutching grand, useless weapon

parts.note: to quake is to tremble

indicators.note: clutching means the word for flee holds the letter inside it

parts.note: to run is to flee
G is slang for a grand, a thousand pounds or dollars

explanation.surface: A frightened person shakes and runs off holding a thousand pounds.
explanation.walkthrough: A useless weapon is a fake one: these painted logs fooled the enemy in the American Civil War.
explanation.definitionFit: A dummy cannon was a log painted to look like artillery, so it could not fire.

clue.text: American nut's wild pogo with a beer

indicators.note: wild says the letters of pogo, a and beer run riot into a new order

explanation.surface: A US crank goes wild on a pogo stick after a beer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wild' mixes up POGO, A and BEER; 'nut' looks like a crank but is a peanut.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a Southern US name for the peanut.

clue.text: One doing circuit judge's area is old

indicators.note: is here tells us the A becomes O, the area is now the old

parts.note: an arbiter is a judge; the possessive adds no letters

explanation.surface: Someone doing a lap of a court circuit, where the judge's district is ancient.
explanation.walkthrough: 'area is old' tells us to change the A of ARBITER into O. 'circuit' looks like a judge's legal circuit but is a path in orbit.
explanation.definitionFit: A spacecraft that circles a planet goes round and round a fixed path.

clue.text: Cannot reveal where this team hides up

indicators.note: up in a down clue means the hidden letters read from bottom to top
hides means the letters sit within the words Cannot reveal

explanation.surface: A secretive person refuses to say where the squad is hiding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hides' finds NOTREVE in 'Cannot reveal', and 'up' turns it around. EVERTON is a Liverpool football club.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a Premier League football club based in Liverpool.

clue.text: In meeting places hard for one to find children's adventure writer

indicators.note: for means hard replaces one, swapping the letters

parts.note: joins are the places where two things meet
I is the Roman numeral one
H is the pencil-grade abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: At meetings, it is hard for someone to track down a writer of kids' books.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hard for one' means H takes the place of I in JOINS.
explanation.definitionFit: Captain W. E. Johns wrote the Biggles adventure books for young readers.

clue.text: God's own judge carrying appeal skyward

indicators.note: skyward in a down clue reads the whole thing upwards
carrying means the first pieces contain the cry

parts.note: to own is to have
oh is a plea or cry of appeal

explanation.surface: God's own judge raises a plea to heaven.
explanation.walkthrough: 'carrying' puts OH inside HAVEJ to give HAVOHEJ, and 'skyward' reads that from the bottom up.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the Old Testament name for the Hebrew deity.

clue.text: English corporal cuts short journey, finding a place to brood

indicators.note: cuts means the soldier pieces cut into the journey

parts.note: a hop is a short trip
a corporal is a non-commissioned officer, NCO

explanation.surface: An English corporal cuts short a trip and finds a quiet place to think.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cuts short' looks like a phrase but is split: 'cuts' is the container signal and 'short journey' is one piece.
explanation.definitionFit: A brooding hen sits on its eggs, and a small shelter for hens is where that happens.

clue.text: Figures making a scene when not allowed to tour meadow

indicators.note: to tour means the forbidden word goes round the meadow

parts.note: tabu is a spelling of taboo, forbidden
lea is a meadow

explanation.surface: Figures make a fuss when banned from touring a meadow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Figures' are posed people, not numbers; TABU is a less common spelling of taboo.
explanation.definitionFit: A tableau vivant is a scene posed by silent motionless people.

clue.text: Let loose in French a curse, audibly

parts.note: un is the French word for a

indicators.note: audibly means the curse is heard rather than spelt

parts.note: damn is a curse

explanation.surface: A Frenchman releases a swear word aloud.
explanation.walkthrough: UN is the French indefinite article. 'audibly' gives DAM, which is said the same as DAMN.
explanation.definitionFit: To remove a barrier from a river releases the water it was holding back.

clue.text: Old character, with an exhortation to peer to return, displays spirit

parts.note: eth is an Old English letter

indicators.note: to return means the exhortation is read backwards

parts.note: lo is an old call to look

explanation.surface: An old figure urges people to look back, and shows high spirits.
explanation.walkthrough: Eth is a letter used in Old English, hence 'Old character'; 'lo' is an old word urging someone to look.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the alcohol in drinks, a distilled spirit.

clue.text: Had spin doctor turned over books, worried?

indicators.note: over means the doctor goes over and around the other pieces
turned means the doctor's letters are reversed

parts.note: OT is the Old Testament, a set of books
something that ate at you worried you

explanation.surface: A political spin doctor turns over the books in a worried state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spin doctor' looks like a political adviser, but 'spin' belongs to the definition and 'doctor' gives DR, which 'turned' makes RD.
explanation.definitionFit: To turn on an axis is to whirl, so went round.

clue.text: Fail — as meters do

definitions.meaning: to stop working, as an engine might

explanation.surface: A gadget breaks down, just like electricity meters.
explanation.definitionFit: To break down is to fail; and meters show readings, so they emit figures.

clue.text: New Irish PM upset with bank's high-risk behaviour

indicators.note: upset means the letters are knocked over into a new order

parts.note: the possessive adds no letters

explanation.surface: A new Irish prime minister is annoyed by the bank's reckless ways.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' rearranges N with IRISHPM and BANK. PM is Prime Minister.
explanation.definitionFit: This is pushing a dangerous situation to the edge to win advantage.
